records.name: Fire
records.description: Chemical energy converted to heat. Unlocks cooking, then metallurgy — the gateway to every refined material above it.

records.name: Lever
records.description: Force traded against distance. The first mechanical advantage; the ancestor of every machine that presses, clamps, or positions.

records.name: Screw
records.description: Rotation converted to controlled translation. Tiny turns become tiny, repeatable movements — precision positioning is born here.

records.name: Gear
records.description: Ratio, torque, and timing between rotating parts. Mechanical regularity — motion that repeats exactly.

records.name: Steel
records.description: Fire plus ore plus control: a material hard enough to cut every material below it. Durable tools, dies, and machine frames.

records.name: Glass
records.description: Melted sand made transparent and shapeable. The substrate of optics, chemistry vessels, and eventually mirror blanks.

records.name: Machining
records.description: Precise removal of material — steel tools guided by screws and gears. Parts made to dimension instead of by eye.

records.name: Micrometer
records.description: A calibrated screw that measures what machining makes. Measurement becomes trustworthy; manufacturing becomes repeatable.

records.name: Lens
records.description: Ground glass that controls light. Microscopes and telescopes reveal hidden worlds; centuries later, its mirror descendants pattern chips.

records.name: Vacuum Pump
records.description: The removal of air itself. Instruments-era machinery that becomes non-negotiable at the summit: EUV light is absorbed by air.

records.name: Generator
records.description: Motion converted to electricity. Energy becomes routable through wires — power exactly where precision needs it.

records.name: Purification
records.description: Removing impurities until the material is the promise. Drugs, water — and silicon pure enough that electrons behave.

records.name: Transistor
records.description: Current controlling current in purified silicon. The switch with no moving parts — computation's atom.

records.name: Laser
records.description: Amplified, coherent light — an oscillator for photons. Powerful enough, aimed at tin droplets, it makes a star in a box.

records.name: Plasma Light Source
records.description: Laser-struck tin plasma emitting extreme ultraviolet photons — light with a wavelength small enough to draw transistors.

records.name: Multilayer Mirror Optics
records.description: No lens passes EUV, so light is steered by atomically-layered mirrors — the lens's descendant, flattered to atomic smoothness.

records.name: Photoresist
records.description: A polymer that remembers light. Where photons land, chemistry changes — the pattern becomes physical.

records.name: Silicon Wafer
records.description: A single crystal grown from purified silicon, sliced and polished — the flattest object most humans will never see.

records.name: Feedback Control
records.description: Compare output to target; correct; repeat. Self-regulation — the only way anything holds position to nanometers.

records.name: EUV Lithography
records.description: Laser, plasma, vacuum, mirrors, resist, wafer, and feedback — every layer of the stick, fused into one machine that mass-produces microscopic computation. From mechanical advantage to matter patterned into thought.
